diagnostic_evidence.quote: the probabilistic result for $c_{\Omega}$ comes directly from taking union bounds on the tail bounds above.

issues.failure_explanation: c_Omega contains max||Omega_j|| twice (once directly, once inside max||Omega_j|| ||Omega_j^{-1}||). The union bounds give max_{i<=d}||Omega_i^{-1}|| <= d sqrt(b)/delta, max_{j>d}||Omega_j^{-1}|| <= (m-d) sqrt(b)/delta, and max_{j>d}||Omega_j|| <= X := 2 sqrt(b) + sqrt(2 log(2(m-d)/delta)). Since b d (m-d) = dn - b d^2, this yields c_Omega^2 <= (dn-bd^2)^3 delta^{-4} X^4. The theorem states the factor X to the first power, which the argument does not give; since X >= 2 the stated bound is strictly stronger and unsupported. The proof's tail bound also contains the typo sqrt(2 log(delta/2)), which is imaginary for delta < 2 (it should be log(2/delta)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the last factor by its fourth power (and fix the log(delta/2) typo in the tail bound). The union-bound argument then proves the corrected statement.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative probability statement for c_Omega^2 is unsupported as written. The deterministic bound (eq:mainsb) is unaffected.
issues.title: High-probability bound on c_Omega^2 has the wrong power of the logarithmic factor
issues.why_classification: A local correction of an exponent, with the same method, probability level and polynomial/log dependence, restores a valid statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notably, $\Lambda$ may consist of either a cluster of interior eigenvalues or a subset of exterior eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma lem:boundMP bounds ||Phi(B_j)|| by the maximum of ||Phi(lambda)|| over the whole interval [lambda_0^(1), lambda_0^(b)] between the extreme eigenvalues of B_j. The proof of thm:sb replaces this by the maximum over [lambda_min, lambda_max] minus the cluster interval, which is a union of two intervals. For j > d, the b eigenvalues in Lambda_j lie outside the cluster interval but may lie on both sides of it. This is exactly the interior-cluster case the paper claims to cover. The hull of the eigenvalues of B_j then contains the cluster interval, where ||Phi(lambda)|| is not controlled by the interpolation bound (thm:interpolation holds only for lambda outside the cluster interval, and G_d takes the maximum only outside). The step is therefore not justified by the lemma as stated.

failure_location.quote: all eigenvalues of $B_{j}$ for $d+1\leq j\leq m$ are in $[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\setminus [\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate lem:boundMP with the maximum over any set containing the eigenvalues of B_0 (e.g. the spectrum, or the two-sided exterior set). The proof already works verbatim for this, since it only evaluates phi_j at the eigenvalues. Then cite this version in thm:sb.
issues.overall_effect: The structural bound (eq:mainsb) is not established for general Lambda_perp (interior clusters, or blocks straddling the cluster). It is established only when each Lambda_j lies on one side of the cluster.
issues.title: Lemma on ||Phi(B_0)|| applied with a maximum over a set that is not the interval it provides, so the interior-cluster case is not covered
issues.why_classification: The existing proof of the lemma already yields the stronger version, so the fix is a short local restatement with no change to the method or conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is, in fact, a necessary condition for the convergence of RSBL

issues.failure_explanation: The chain begins by equating dim(range(Q~) ∩ K_ell) with dim range(Q~ Q~^T K_ell), the dimension of the projection of the Krylov space onto the eigenspace. In general only '<=' holds. A vector in both spaces satisfies v = Q~ Q~^T v, so the intersection lies inside the projected space, but the projected space can be much larger. Example: ell = 1 with generic Omega, where the intersection is {0} while Q~ Q~^T Omega has rank b. The conclusion (at most b dimensions) still follows from '<=', but the displayed equalities are false and the needed inclusion is not argued.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first equality by '<=' and add the one-line argument that v in range(Q~) ∩ K_ell implies v = Q~ Q~^T v lies in range(Q~ Q~^T K_ell).
issues.overall_effect: The justification that multiplicity larger than b obstructs convergence is incorrectly written. The conclusion survives with the inequality.
issues.title: Necessity argument uses a false dimension equality
issues.why_classification: A short local repair preserves the claim and its scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $d = 1$, \cref{cor:eig} recovers the convergence result for randomized single-vector Lanczos method

issues.failure_explanation: thm:sb gives tan angle <= c_Omega G_d with G_d <= (chi_m chi_c / gap)^{d-1}. The prefactor c_Omega (of order sqrt(n)) can be absorbed into the (d-1)-th power only if d >= 2. For d = 1 the stated bound reads tan angle <= 1, which is false for b = 1 and Gaussian Omega, where tan angle(e_1, omega) is typically of order sqrt(n). Likewise (cor:eig) at d = 1 gives 1/Cheb_{ell-1}(.) with no initial-angle factor. The claim that it 'recovers' the single-vector theorem is therefore wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound as c_{b,d,n} (c'_{b,d}/gap)^{d-1}, or restrict to d >= 2. Adjust the d = 1 recovery statement and (cor:eig) accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary and the eigenvalue-computation consequence (cor:eig) are incorrect for d = 1 and do not recover the cited single-vector result there. They are valid only for d >= 2 (and conditionally on the conjecture).
issues.title: Conjectural corollary has exponent d-1 that removes the prefactor; false at d=1, yet claimed to recover the single-vector result
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local change of form (prefactor outside the power) that keeps the conjectured rate and the conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this simple situation, $\chim$ can be bounded using existing results from random matrix theory

issues.failure_explanation: For d = 2, chi_mono is controlled by ratios ||lambda I - B_i|| / ||lambda I - Lambda_i|| with B_i = Omega_i^{-1} Lambda_i Omega_i. This is bounded by kappa(Omega_i) = ||Omega_i|| ||Omega_i^{-1}||, not by the condition number of B_i. Counterexample: B_2 = [[1,t],[0,1+eps]] with t = 10, eps = 0.01, Lambda_2 = diag(1, 1+eps), and lambda_min^cl = 1 (allowed, since the cluster interval is the hull of the eigenvalues). The ratio is about t/eps = 1000, while ||B_2|| ||B_2^{-1}|| is about 100 (taking B_1 = diag(2,3) as the other block). The stated inequality fails, and a condition number of the nonsymmetric B_i is not what the cited random-matrix results (Gaussian Omega_i) control.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||B_i|| ||B_i^{-1}|| by ||Omega_i|| ||Omega_i^{-1}|| (the eigenvector-matrix condition number) and bound it with the Rudelson–Vershynin tail bounds already used.
issues.overall_effect: The assertion that chi_mono is handled by existing random matrix results is unsupported as written. The identification of the difficulty with chi_c is unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed bound chi_mono <= max ||B_i|| ||B_i^{-1}|| is false (should involve eigenvector-matrix condition numbers)
issues.why_classification: A two-line local correction with the same conclusion (chi_mono is controlled by Gaussian condition numbers) preserves all substantive claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Plugging \cref{conj:sb} into \cite[Thm.~2]{Meyer2023}, we know that when
is bounded by a constant depending on $b$ and $d$

issues.failure_explanation: The low-rank bound (cor:lr) is derived by inserting the conjectured corollary conj:sb (itself resting on the unproven conj:chi), not the proven thm:sb. The constant c_{b,d,n} is only said to depend on b, d, n with no growth control. Linear scaling of the matvec count b*ell in the target rank bd needs log c_{b,d,n} to stay bounded or very slowly growing in b and d, which neither the conjecture nor the theorem provides. The sentence asserts the literature conjecture is achieved, whereas only a conditional and quantitatively unspecified statement is derived.

failure_location.quote: As a consequence, it achieves the conjecture

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim as conditional on Conjecture 1 and on a stated growth bound for log c_{b,d,n} in b and d; otherwise present it only as consistent with the cited conjecture.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised resolution of the matvec-complexity conjecture is not established. At most a conditional consequence of an unproven conjecture is shown.
issues.title: Claim that the paper 'achieves' the Meyer–Musco–Musco conjecture rests on an unproven conjecture with uncontrolled constants
issues.why_classification: The repair weakens the advertised consequence to a conditional one, a limited weakening that leaves a comparable (conditional) result without new proof architecture.
